words.ex: Its color is blue.
words.en: Belonging to or associated with a thing previously mentioned or easily identified.

words.ex: Our dog sleeps on the floor.
words.en: Belonging to or associated with the speaker and one or more other people previously mentioned or easily identified.

words.tr: pron. 他们的；她们的；它们的；
words.ex: Their books are on the table.
words.en: You use their to indicate that something belongs or relates to the group of people, animals, or things that you are talking about.

words.ex: The cat is under the table.
words.en: In or to a position below or beneath something.

words.tr:
prep. 在…后面；
adv. 在后面；
words.ex: The cat is behind the sofa.
words.en: If something is behind a thing or person, it is on the far side of them as they face you, or is in a back part of them.

words.ex: The cat is sitting in front of the house.
words.en: If someone or something is in front of a particular thing, they are facing it, ahead of it, or close to the front part of it.

words.ex: He sat beside his friend on the bus.
words.en: At the side of; next to.

words.ex: I like tea or coffee.
words.en: You use or to link two or more alternatives.

words.tr:
conj. 但是；然而；
prep. 除…以外；
adv. 只能；仅仅；
words.ex: I like apples, but I don't like oranges.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢苹果，但是我不喜欢橙子。
words.en: used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting with what has already been mentioned

words.ex: He was late because the bus was slow.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，因为公交车很慢。
words.en: You use 'because' when stating the reason for something.

words.ex: Although it was raining, he went outside.
words.ex_cn: 虽然天下雨了，他还是出去了。
words.en: Despite the fact that; even though.

words.tr:
conj. 虽然；尽管；然而；
adv. 虽然；尽管；可是；
words.ex: Though it was raining, he went out.
words.ex_cn: 虽然天下雨了，他还是出去了。
words.en: You use though to introduce a statement in a subordinate clause which contrasts with the statement in the main clause. You often use though to introduce a fact which you regard as less important than the fact in the main clause.

words.ex: If it rains, we will stay home.
words.ex_cn: 如果下雨，我们就待在家里。
words.en: You use if in conditional sentences to introduce the circumstances in which an event or situation might happen, might be happening, or might have happened.

words.ex: I am eating now.
words.en: at the present time or moment

words.tr:
adv. 然后；接下来；那时；
adj. 当时的；那时的；
words.ex: I ate breakfast, then I went to school.
words.ex_cn: 我吃了早餐，然后去了学校。
words.en: At that time; next in order of time; in that case.

words.ex: He will arrive soon.
words.en: If something is going to happen soon, it will happen after a short time. If something happened soon after a particular time or event, it happened a short time after it.

words.tr:
adv. 在今天；当今；
n. 今天；当今；
words.ex: I will finish my homework today.
words.ex_cn: 我今天会完成我的作业。
words.en: This day, as distinct from yesterday or tomorrow.

words.tr:
adv. 昨天；
n. 昨天；
words.ex: I saw her yesterday.
words.en: The day before today.

words.tr:
n. 明天；
adv. 在明天；
words.ex: I will go to school tomorrow.
words.en: The day after today; in the future.

words.tr:
adv. 如此；这么；很；也
conj. 所以
words.ex: I am so tired after school.
words.en: used to emphasize the degree or extent of something

words.ex: It is quite cold today.
words.en: To a certain or fairly significant extent or degree; fairly.

words.tr: adv. 更确切地说；宁可；相当；
words.ex: I don't like coffee; rather, I prefer tea.
words.ex_cn: 我不喜欢咖啡；更确切地说，我更喜欢茶。
words.en: You use rather to indicate that something is true to a fairly great extent, especially when you are talking about something unpleasant or undesirable.

words.ex: He always eats breakfast at 7 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他总是在早上七点吃早餐。
words.en: At all times; on all occasions.

words.ex: She usually walks to school.
words.en: Under normal conditions; generally.

words.ex: He often goes to the park after school.
words.en: Many times; frequently.

words.ex: I sometimes walk to school.
words.en: At times; occasionally.

words.ex: He seldom eats fast food.
words.en: If something seldom happens, it happens only occasionally.

words.ex: He has never been to Japan.
words.en: At no time in the past or future; on no occasion; not ever.

words.tr:
pron. 这个；
adj. 这；
adv. 这样；这个；这么；
words.ex: This is my book.
words.en: You use 'this' to refer to a person or thing that is near you, especially when you touch them or point to them.

words.tr:
conj. 那（引导从句）；
pron. 那儿；那里；
adj. 那；那个；那样的；
adv. 那个；那么；那样；
words.ex: I know that he is coming tomorrow.
words.en: Used to identify a specific person or thing observed or heard by the speaker.

words.tr: pron. 这些；“this”的复数； adj. 这些的；
words.ex: These books are on the table.
words.en: You use these at the beginning of noun groups to refer to someone or something that you have already mentioned or identified.

words.tr: pron. 那些；“that”的复数； adj. 那些的；
words.ex: Those books are on the table.
words.en: You use those to refer to people or things which have already been mentioned or which are already known about.

words.ex: I did it myself.
words.en: Used by a speaker to refer to himself or herself as the object of a verb or preposition when he or she is the subject of the clause.

words.ex: You should believe in yourself.
words.en: Used to refer to the person being addressed as the object of a verb or preposition when they are also the subject of the clause.

words.ex: He cleaned the room himself.
words.en: used as the object of a verb or preposition when the male subject of the verb is also the object

words.ex: She cleaned the room herself.
words.en: Used as the object of a verb or preposition when the female subject of the verb is also the object.

words.ex: The dog licked itself.
words.en: Used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to a thing or animal previously mentioned as the subject of the clause.

words.ex: We cleaned the house ourselves.
words.en: Used as the object of a verb or preposition when this is the same as the subject of the clause and the subject is the speaker and one or more other people considered together.

words.ex: You should clean your room yourselves.
words.ex_cn: 你们应该自己打扫房间。
words.en: Used as the object of a verb or preposition when this is the same as the subject of the clause and the subject is you.

words.tr: pron. 他们自己；她们自己；它们自己；
words.ex: The children cleaned the room themselves.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们自己打扫了房间。
words.en: Used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to a group of people or things previously mentioned as the subject of the clause.

words.ex: He studied hard so that he could pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以便通过考试。
words.en: Used to introduce a clause of purpose or result.

words.tr:
conj. 在…的时候；
adv. 什么时候；
words.ex: I eat breakfast when I wake up.
words.en: You use when to ask about the time that something happened or will happen.

words.tr:
conj. 当…的时候；尽管；然而；
n. 一段时间；一会儿；
words.ex: I read a book while I waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 我等公交车的时候读了一本书。
words.en: While is used to introduce a clause in which you mention something that happens at the same time as something else, or to introduce a clause that contrasts with something else that you have mentioned.

words.tr:
prep. 在…之后；
adv. 以后；后来；
words.ex: I will call you after dinner.
words.en: In addition to its use as a preposition meaning 'behind in place or time,' 'after' can also function as an adverb to indicate a subsequent time or event.

words.tr:
prep. 在…之前；先于；
conj. 在…以前；
adv. 以前；之前；
words.ex: She ate breakfast before school.
words.ex_cn: 她在上学之前吃了早餐。
words.en: Earlier in time; previously.

words.ex: There is a book on the table.
words.en: Used to indicate the place where someone or something is or where something happens.

words.tr:
n. 家；家庭；
adv. 在家；
adj. 家的；家庭的；
words.ex: I love to go home after work.
words.en: The place where one lives permanently, especially as a member of a family or household.

words.ex: He went abroad to study medicine.
words.en: In or to a foreign country or countries.

words.tr: adv. 到处；处处；各个地方；所有地方；
words.ex: She looked everywhere for her keys.
words.en: in or to all places

words.tr: adv. 然而；不过；不论到什么程度；无论如何；
words.ex: I like coffee; however, I drink tea in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢咖啡；然而，我早上喝茶。
words.en: You use however when you are adding a comment which is surprising or which contrasts with what has just been said.

words.ex: It rained all day, therefore the game was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 下了一整天的雨，因此比赛被取消了。
words.en: You use therefore to introduce a logical result or conclusion.

words.tr: adv. 否则；在其他方面；除此之外；
words.ex: Hurry up, otherwise you'll be late.
words.en: in circumstances different from those present or considered; or else

words.ex: Where is the book?
words.en: You use where to ask questions about the place or position of someone or something, or to indicate the place or position of someone or something.

words.ex: Why did you come late?
words.en: You use why in questions when you ask about the reasons for something.

words.ex: How do you make coffee?
words.en: In what way or manner; by what means.

words.ex: She could swim when she was five.
words.en: Used to indicate possibility or ability in the past, or to make a polite request.

words.ex: My birthday is in May.
words.en: May is the fifth month of the Gregorian calendar, following April and preceding June.

words.tr: v. 可能；也许；“may”的过去式； n. 强大力量；
words.ex: He might come to the party tonight.
words.ex_cn: 他今晚可能会来参加派对。
words.en: Might is used to indicate that something is possible or might happen, or to ask for permission in a polite way.

words.tr:
auxv. 必须；一定要；
n. 必须做的事；必不可少的事物；
words.ex: You must finish your homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 你必须在晚饭前完成作业。
words.en: Used to indicate that something is very likely or certain to be true or to happen.

words.ex: You should eat more vegetables.
words.en: You use 'should' when you are saying what would be the right thing to do or the right state for something to be in.
